title: GitLab week 5 review - building, publishing and structuring
description: Eight questions on images, the registry, cache, templates and merge request pipelines.

questions.prompt: Why does a docker-executor job need a docker:dind service to run docker build?

options.text: The job is itself a container with no daemon; dind provides one next to it
It does not - docker build works without it

questions.explanation: Alternatives: kaniko (no daemon) or a shell runner's host daemon.

questions.prompt: Which credentials log a job into the project's registry, and how long is the password valid?

options.text: CI_REGISTRY_USER / CI_REGISTRY_PASSWORD (the job token); only while the job runs

questions.explanation: The job token is minted per job and dies with it.

questions.prompt: Why deploy by image SHA rather than :latest?

options.text: An immutable tag is traceable to a commit and makes rollback reproducible; :latest moves

questions.explanation: Build once, promote the same artifact by SHA.

questions.prompt: With npm ci, why cache .npm/ instead of node_modules/?

options.text: npm ci deletes node_modules before installing; caching npm's download cache is what speeds it up

questions.explanation: Cache the download cache, keyed on the lock file.

questions.prompt: A required file is in cache and the job fails when the cache is empty. What is the design error?

options.text: An artifact is pretending to be a cache - cache is best effort, artifacts are guaranteed

questions.explanation: Cache speeds things up; it must never be required for correctness.

questions.prompt: Two jobs extend .node; one sets its own before_script. Does the template's before_script run too?

options.text: No - extends merges maps and the job's key replaces the template's

questions.explanation: Use !reference [.node, before_script] to splice it in explicitly.

questions.prompt: What does the Full configuration tab in the pipeline editor show?

options.text: The YAML after includes, templates and extends are expanded

questions.explanation: It is where you debug 'where does this job come from'.

questions.prompt: What does a merged results pipeline test that a plain MR pipeline does not?

options.text: The result of merging source into target

questions.explanation: A source branch can be green and still break main; merged results catch that.
